verdict.rationale: GitHub's own docs show that fine-grained personal access tokens are created with a chosen set of permissions that define which resources the token can reach via the API. The X-Accepted-GitHub-Permissions response header tells you which permissions an endpoint requires, which supports least-privilege scoping. The evidence does not tie these tokens to agent use or detail how far scoping goes, so coverage is partial. missing for 10: documentation of agent-specific credential issuance (e.g., credentials for Copilot or MCP agents), evidence of per-repository/resource scoping, expiration and revocation controls, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: When you create a fine-grained personal access token, you grant it a set of permissions. Permissions define what resources the token can access via the API.
The header will tell you what permissions are required in order to access the endpoint.
